high.title: Selic Rate Expected to Fall, But How Far Can COPOM Go? 17 Institutions Share Their Forecasts
high.summary: Brazil's Monetary Policy Committee (COPOM) is set to announce its interest rate decision today (August 5th), with the overwhelming consensus pointing toward a continuation of the monetary easing cycle. Of 17 banks and brokerages surveyed by Money Times, 16 expect a 25 basis point cut, bringing the Selic rate down from 14.25% to 14.00% per annum. The sole dissenter is Citi, which projects the BCB will hold rates steady at 14.25%, reflecting a more cautious view on the pace of easing.

high.title: Selic Falls to 14%, but It's Petrobras (PETR4) Moving Markets; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Rises Today (6)
high.summary:
The Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) delivered a widely anticipated 25 basis point rate cut at its latest COPOM meeting, lowering the Selic from 14.25% to 14.00% per annum. Critically, the BCB adopted a notably cautious tone in its accompanying statement, deliberately avoiding forward guidance on the pace or direction of future cuts — a signal that the easing cycle will be measured and data-dependent. Despite the lack of explicit guidance, market economists interpreted the statement constructively, noting that the BCB acknowledged a **gradual deceleration in economic activity** and **improvement in near-term inflation dynamics** at the margin. These are conditions that could open the door to further cuts if sustained. Meanwhile, Petrobras (PETR4) is emerging as the dominant market-moving force today, overshadowing the rate decision itself, with the Ibovespa rising in USD terms. **Key takeaways for traders:** The cautious BCB tone should limit aggressive re-pricing of the short end of the yield curve. Watch the DI futures curve for any flattening. BRL reaction will hinge on whether the dovish cut is offset by Petrobras-driven equity inflows supporting the currency. Next COPOM meeting and IPCA prints are the critical catalysts to monitor.

medium.title: Petrobras (PETR4): What to Expect from Earnings? Dividends Back in Focus
medium.summary:
Petrobras (PETR4) is set to release its Q2 2026 results after market close today (August 6), with analyst consensus projecting net revenue of R$30.8 billion. The quarter is expected to show sequential improvement, driven by record oil and gas production, higher commodity prices, and improved refining margins — all of which should support a stronger earnings print. Dividends are back at the center of investor attention, making this a pivotal event for capital flows into Brazilian equities. For BRL and Ibovespa traders, a strong Petrobras result with a generous dividend announcement could attract foreign portfolio inflows, providing a supportive tailwind for the Real. Given Petrobras's outsized weight in the Ibovespa index, any earnings surprise — positive or negative — will have a disproportionate impact on index performance and sentiment across the broader Brazilian equity market today.
